SourceActivities: 9.1 Notice and Wonder Dots in a Square
9.2 Who Is Closest? three and four sites, allocation and ties
9.3 optional expanded dynamic Voronoi with letter

Task.Prompt: On original paper square-city map, partition nearest regions for A=(0,0), B=(8,0), C=(0,6), then add D=(8,6). Label all bisector boundaries, triple ties and write which additional evidence would be required to allocate 100 staff. Show one original grid tessellation and derived nearest-site cells.

Criteria.Criterion: nearest-site bisectors for 3 labelled stores correct
fourth store update and tie cases labelled
staffing assumptions and valid argument with limitation

Items.Prompt: How can you compare which of two sites A and B is closer to a point X?
Items.Expected: Construct the perpendicular bisector AB, locate X on the closer half-plane or tie boundary.

Items.Prompt: A point is on the perpendicular bisector of AB. Is it nearer A or B?
Items.Expected: Equal distance; the point lies on the Voronoi boundary.

Items.Prompt: Three stores at (0,0),(8,0),(0,6) have a common triple-tie point. Locate it.
How can you make an isosceles triangle ABC from base AB?
Items.Expected: Take C on perpendicular bisector of AB but not on AB, so AC=BC.

Items.Prompt: Which conditions define a regular polygon?
Items.Expected: At least three sides; all side lengths equal and all interior angles congruent.

Items.Prompt: What completes a rectangle after constructing two perpendiculars to AB at A and B?
Items.Expected: Mark C on the perpendicular at A, construct a line through C parallel AB, meet B's perpendicular at D and join.

Items.Prompt: Why do two equal-radius arcs from points B,D constrain the bisector of angle BAD?
Items.Expected: Equal distance from marks on both rays plus common vertex establishes symmetric triangles and equal angles.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: explain why the site at (4,3) is equally distant from three stores and why equal-area alone cannot determine staff counts
PaperDelivery: Student submits labelled map and justification to teacher offline; teacher checks geometry, scores each criterion 0/1/2, signs/dates feedback sheet. No live upload/persisted grade claimed.

Cases.CORRECT: proper cells and tie lines and demand caveat
Cases.EQUIVALENT: translated/rotated coordinate maps, other valid polygon intersection methods
Cases.WRONG: incorrect nearest-site region or staffing numbers claimed from area without assumptions
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: unlabelled colored regions or numeric answer without diagram
Cases.MALFORMED: coincident sites treated as distinct, undefined region
